articles.title: A picture of violence: The 31 women killed in Northern Ireland since 2020
articles.summary: In at least 22 of the 31 deaths, the killers - or the suspects in their killings - were well-known to the women.
articles.body:
Since 2020, 31 women have been violently killed in Northern Ireland.

Each one of them was a daughter, the majority of them mothers.

They were sisters, aunts, friends and some of them were grandmothers.

All but one of these women were killed by a man or it is a man who has been charged in connection with their deaths.

In each case, for the women's families and friends, the trauma of their deaths will be felt forever and be passed down to the next generation.

In at least 22 of the deaths, the killers - or the suspects in their killings - were well-known to the women.

That figure could be higher as the relationship to some of those accused of the killings is not yet known.

The cases are still going through the legal process.

Those that have been accused or convicted of the killings include husbands, partners, ex-partners, brothers, sons, a friend and a grandson.

At least 22 of the women were attacked or killed in their own homes.

Another, Katie Brankin, was killed while on a glamping holiday.

The exact details of the properties where some of the women died have not yet been confirmed.

The women who have been killed ranged in age from their 20s to their 80s.

The youngest was Patrycja Wryebek, who was 20.

Elizabeth Dobbin was 82 when she was killed in her Larne home.

At least 22 of the women were mothers. Natalie McNally and Sarah Montgomery were pregnant when they were killed.

In four cases, the women’s children were present at the properties where they were attacked.

Each of these women have left behind heartbroken families.

Families who want their loved one remembered for the lives they had and not their violent deaths.

Betty Dobbin was known to her great granddaughter as “Great Dobbin”, a term of affection which her family said showed her importance within the entire family circle.

One week after the first coronavirus lockdown came into force, the 82-year-old’s body was discovered at her home in Larne.

She had been strangled before being subjected to a "serious blunt force assault”.

Mrs Dobbin was killed by her 32-year-old grandson who shared a house with her.

In a police confession Alan Gingles described "seeing zombies" with his grandmother.

After medical evidence was put before the court, he was re-arraigned and pleaded guilty to manslaughter by means of diminished responsibility.

He was handed down an indeterminate prison sentence with a minimum tariff of five years.

Natasha Melendez’s mother said of her daughter: “You wanted to love and be loved deeply and you loved your children with all of your heart.”

Ms Melendez was a mother-of-four living in Lisburn. She was originally from Venezuela.

She was attacked in her home by her partner on 22 March 2020 and died 10 days later in hospital.

Thirty-five-year-old John David Scott pleaded guilty to her murder and to three prior physical attacks. He was handed a life sentence.

Emma Jane McParland was at home on the Ormeau Road in Belfast with two friends when her son attacked her.

Jordan Kennedy stabbed her five times with a kitchen knife. Her friends tried to help her but she was pronounced dead a short time later.

Described in court as “an important and much loved figure” she had tried to get help for her son who had “complex needs”.

Kennedy, who was 21 at the time, admitted murdering his mother. He told police he believed she was in a relationship with one or more of his friends.

Kennedy was sentenced to a minimum of 14 years in prison.

Patrycja Wyrebek was strangled and beaten to death by her partner in her Newry home.

The 20-year-old was the eldest of five. Her family had moved from Poland to Northern Ireland when she was a young child.

They said they were overwhelmed by grief: "Our children are the only thing that gives us something to live for. Our hearts are broken and we will never be the same again”.

Ms Wyrebek had moved in with David Lukasz Mietus eight months before her murder.

Mietus was arrested near their home holding a knife to his throat.

He pleaded guilty to murder and was sentenced to at least 20 years in prison.

Ms Wyrebek had previously reported Mietus to the police for domestic violence.

Katie Simpson was a talented showjumper, being with horses was her “happy place”.

One of six children, she was a much loved daughter, sister, granddaughter and a devoted aunt.

Her sister Rebecca said her defining memory of Ms Simpson was the joy that shone from her as she rode her ponies.

"She was a joy, a light, absolutely fearless - she could walk into any room and she'd have the best time," Rebecca said.

In August 2020, Ms Simpson was beaten and strangled to death.

Jonathan Creswell, who was in a relationship with one of Katie’s sisters, initially told police she had tried to take her own life. She died in hospital six days later.

Creswell was later charged with her murder. He was found dead at his home on the second day of his trial in April 2024.

Susan Baird was described as a “much-loved sister and mother”.

One of her children wrote: “On 16 August 2020 my dad killed my mum. This will never get any easier to say for me.

"I struggle to write it, never mind say it aloud and I still find it extremely hard to believe this is our reality.”

Mrs Baird's body was found slumped on a sofa in their home.

She had been beaten to death with a hammer.

Her husband of nearly 40 years called the police and told them he had killed his wife.

Gary Baird pleaded guilty to manslaughter by means of diminished responsibility and was handed a seven year sentence.

During the trial it was heard that Baird called his GP more than 500 times for help, none of his calls were answered.

Karen McClean was killed in her home in March 2021 as part of a double killing.

The body of her son’s girlfriend was later found in a house nearby .

At the time, the police commented that the deaths of the two women in County Antrim had "left children facing a lifetime without their mums".

Ms McClean was found dead in her Newtownabbey home. She had been stabbed.

Police believe she was murdered by her son, Ken Flanagan.

Flanagan went on to kill Stacey Knell and then take his own life.

Her family described "a huge void" being left in their lives following her death.

They said the loss of Ms Knell had caused “unimaginable pain" but their priority was to care for her daughter.

Ms Knell’s friends raised thousands of pounds to help pay for the funeral costs.

“A quiet lady who kept to herself," Ludmila Poletelova worked in a local wine bar in Limavady and had a small group of friends.

She came to Northern Ireland in 2009 and after getting settled she helped fellow Latvians and eastern Europeans who were struggling.

Ms Poletelova was killed in her Limavady home by her friend Svetlana Svedova.

She hit her more than 50 times with a claw hammer.

Svedova was jailed for at least 16 years after pleading guilty to murder.

Ms Poletelova had two sons whom she was close to and spoke to regularly.

One of her sons said his mother’s murder had had a "devastating impact" on the family.

The local community raised thousands of pounds towards the cost of repatriating Ms Poletelova’s remains back to Latvia.

It was the July bank holiday and Katie Brankin had gone away for a break to a glamping site in County Londonderry with her partner and baby.

An inquest into the Newtownabbey woman’s death heard that she was stabbed multiple times. She died outside their campervan.

Her partner, Thomas Davidson, admitted the killing during police interviews.

He died in Maghaberry prison six weeks later while on remand, charged with the murder of the mother-of-one.

"I'm just so sorry my children have seen this but I love them so much."

Katrina Rainey uttered the phrase to emergency services at the scene where she was fatally injured.

The mother-of-six was being helped by her children, who were placing wet towels on her burnt body when fire crews arrived.

She was described by her mother as a "gentle, sincere, beautiful girl that made time for everyone".

Ms Rainey was preparing to go to work when her husband, Thomas Rainey, opened her car door, threw petrol over her and set her alight.

Rainey pleaded guilty to her murder and will spend at least 18 years of his life sentence in prison.

A much loved daughter, sister, sister-in-law and aunt, Caoimhe Morgan was remembered as always smiling, happy and outgoing.

The mum-of-four was murdered just days before Christmas.

Two of her four young children were in the house at the time, one was said to have been found “trying to comfort his mother’s lifeless body”.

Ms Morgan’s mother discovered her body. She had been beaten to death with a blunt instrument.

Taylor George McIlvenna had been in a relationship with Caoimhe Morgan for six years.

He pleaded guilty to her murder and must spend at least 17 years in prison.

He had an extensive criminal recording including prior offences of domestic violence.

Alyson Nelson had taken care of people her entire life.

The 64-year-old retired nurse had cared for her mother and her husband - the father of the youngest of her four children - as he died of cancer.

Following her death, 300 people attended a vigil along the seafront in the County Antrim town of Whitehead.

Her family said they had taken "great comfort" from knowing "how loved mum was and still is by her friends, her family and all those who stand with us".

Ms Nelson was stabbed seven times in her home by her ex-partner William Finlay, who she had met online.

Finlay pleaded guilty to murder was told he must serve at least 20 years in prison.

He was the first person in Northern Ireland to be convicted of murder aggravated by domestic abuse. He had previous convictions for domestic violence.

She was the grandmother who spoiled her grandson and the woman that family went to for advice.

She was found dead in bed in her Cookstown home on 19 June with her rosary beads in her hands.

A preliminary post-mortem found the 77-year-old died after being strangled.

Her son Barry Noone, who shared an address with her, was arrested at the scene.

Noone admitted he was responsible for her death but denied murder.

He later admitted the charge of manslaughter on the grounds of diminished responsibility which was accepted by the Crown due to his mental state at the time.

In December 2024 he was sentenced to six years in prison, three to be spent in custody and three on licence.

A dedicated and popular class-room assistant and devoted mother to her three-year-old daughter, Hollie Thomson’s “big laugh meant that you would hear her before you saw her".

At her funeral Mass, the priest said: “Hollie was a young woman who touched the lives of very, very many people as evidenced by the huge crowd of people here today.

"She had a beautiful and unforgettable smile that radiated so much kindness and warmth".

Ms Thomson was found dead at her home off Shaws Road in Belfast.

Preliminary examinations identified suffocation and a fractured neck as the possible cause of death.

Her partner Christopher Morelli was charged with her murder.

While on bail, his body was found at a property in Hillsborough. The death was not treated as suspicious.

Natalie McNally was known as "Nats" at home.

Her brother Niall said she was the best sister and that he and his two brothers had treated her like a princess.

A lover of animals, Ms McNally’s mother described her as strong, fiercely independent and hardworking and the best daughter that you could wish for.

She was 15 weeks pregnant when she was killed.

Ms McNally’s body was discovered in her Lurgan home shortly before Christmas 2022 - she had sustained stab wounds and compression to the neck, as well as blunt force wounds to the head.

Her partner Stephen McCullagh was charged with her murder and a four week trial began in February 2026.

After two hours of deliberation in March the jury found him guilty and in June 2026 he was sentenced to at least 31 years in prison.

Alesia Nazarova and her partner had planned to marry. He said he thinks about her every day.

Her family said their hearts were broken and they would never be the same.

Ms Nazarova was found dead following a house fire in Portadown. A girl who was in the house was rescued by firefighters.

The local community raised thousands of pounds to help the young girl.

Ms Nazarova's brother Kornelijus Bracas whom she had shared the house with, pleaded guilty to her murder and arson endangering the life of the 12-year old girl.

In passing down a sentence of 24 years the judge described Bracas as "one of the most brutal, cold-blooded murderers" she has come across.

Ms Nazarova was strangled and stabbed before her brother set the house on fire. She was still alive when the fires were lit.

Ms Nazarova and her brother were both originally from Lithuania.

In the words of her older sister Nadine, Chloe Mitchell was “a real wee party popper”.

Standing amongst a sea of flowers alongside her brother, she said “my sister will always be living while I am, because she had half of my heart and I currently have half of hers".

Ms Mitchell was last seen on CCTV in the early hours 3 June in Ballymena town centre.

Her remains were found eight days later in a flat in the town.

Brandon Rainey, 29, of James Street in Ballymena, has been charged with her murder and attempting to prevent the lawful and decent burial of a deceased body.

In a family tribute Kat Parton was described as "a precious daughter and devoted mother who loved her son with every bone in her body".

Police believe Ms Parton was attacked on 9 May, but only discovered six days later when her father went to check on her.

He found his daughter’s body in the bedroom of her home in Madrid Street in Belfast. She had severe head injuries.

During a vigil, one friend remembered: "We danced together and she lit up every room and was full of life.”

Her partner Jamie Love, 23, is charged with her murder, the offence aggravated by domestic abuse. He remains in custody.

A retired school teacher and grandmother, Patsy Aust's focus was always her family.

The congregation at her funeral service heard Ms Aust would be missed for her “kindness and love” and her “desire to keep going with deep resilience and fortitude”.

Her standing in her community shone through in her death notice.

"Only the best memories of you Patsy and the happiness you have brought to us all," it read.

"You will never be forgotten, and we shall try to support ourselves with our memories of having you to cherish and love."

Ms Aust’s body was found at a house in Bangor, County Down.

Sophie Watson, who was 57, was found dead at a property in Ashgrove Park in Magherafelt, County Londonderry.

Women’s Aid Northern Ireland expressed their deepest condolences to Ms Watson’s loved ones following her death.

Andrzej Pajaczkowski of Ashgrove Park has been charged with her murder.

He replied “not guilty” when the charge was put to him. He remains in custody.

Firefighters found the remains of Montserrat Elias.

She was 66 and was originally from Spain but had been living in Londonderry.

It took police some time to identify Ms Elias.

They said she had suffered multiple injuries from an unspecified weapon during a "horrific attack" before a ground floor flat was set on fire.

Dozens of people attended a vigil in her memory at Derry’s Guildhall Square.

One of the organisers spoke of the sadness felt by many in the city.

Ciaran Murray, 28, from Gortfoyle Place, has been charged with murder and arson with intent to endanger life. He remains in custody. He has pleaded not guilty to murder.

During a service of thanksgiving, Rachel Simpson's sister Cher described her as “full of beans, funny faces, and warm embraces”.

She added: “Rachel was a cherished mother of three much-loved children. This love remains eternal.”

Ms Simpson had started two successful businesses.

Her body was discovered in a garage on the Castlereagh Road in Belfast.

Her 21-year-old son Nathan Simpson has been charged with her murder.

During a court hearing, it was heard that he had been released from prison seven days before her death.

In December 2025 he was transferred to a high-security state psychiatric hospital in South Lanarkshire for medical assessment.

In her death notice Mary Ward, who was a mother-of-one was described as a “beloved daughter”, “much loved mummy” and “loving sister” to five brothers and sisters.

Her body was discovered by police officers at her home in Melrose Street in south Belfast on 1 October 2024.

In a press conference the police said: "We observed a female crouched over against the upstairs front window of that house and located Mary deceased unfortunately within the property."

Police believe Ms Ward was last seen alive on 25 September.

A murder investigation was begun six days after her remains were found.

Ahmed Abdirahman, with an address at Kinlay House in Dame Street, Dublin, has been charged in court in Dublin with her murder.

Ms Ward had made a complaint to the Police Service of Northern Ireland on 4 September about being the victim of violence.

Karen Cummings was a children's nurse and mother of two.

She was found unconscious with a serious head injury at her Banbridge home and later died there.

One person who left a floral tribute at the scene said they had not known Karen well, but that she had looked after one of their family members at hospital recently and was full of "bounce" on the ward.

Two men have appeared in court charged with manslaughter.

They are Glenn King, 32, of no fixed address in Lurgan and 42-year-old Kevin McGuigan Jnr of Annacloy Park in Hillsborough. They both deny the charges.

Mary Green - known as Marie - was found dead in her home in north Belfast.

A neighbour described her as a "lovely lady" and local politicians said the incident was "absolutely heartbreaking".

Her son, Lewis Green, was charged with her murder, he remains in custody.

Sarah Montgomery was a mother of two young girls and pregnant with her third child when she died at her home in Donaghadee.

She was found unconscious and seriously injured when police and paramedics arrived at her home. Medical treatment was provided but she died.

A tribute left outside her home described her as a "beautiful, kind and wonderful mother". She had planned to call her son Liam Arthur.

Zak Hughes, 28, of Ardglen Place in north Belfast, pleaded guilty to her murder and also a charge of child destruction in June 2026.

The judge said she would impose a life sentence. He will be sentenced in September.

A 42-year-old woman who was arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender, was released unconditionally.

Veterinary surgeon Vanessa Whyte, 45, was shot dead alongside her 14-year-old son James and 13-year-old daughter Sara at their home outside Maguiresbridge, County Fermanagh.

In the words of one of her sisters, Vanessa and her two children were "taken from this world in a cruel and vicious manner".

The man suspected of the killings was 43-year-old Ian Rutledge. He was taken from the scene to hospital with gunshot wounds.

He was Ms Whyte's husband and the father of her two children. He died days later.

Ms Whyte and her two children were buried together in her home town of Barefield, County Clare.

In her eulogy, Vanessa's sister spoke of her family's heartbreak.

"We as a family have been robbed of both a relationship with our sister and a chance to see James and Sara grow up, and they have been robbed of the remainder of their lives."

Police said a suspected triple murder and attempted suicide was one line of inquiry for detectives.

Ellie Flanagan was described as a "well loved and respected" young woman who "brought a lot of light and joy into this world".

An enthusiastic cast member in local pantomimes, she also worked in childcare and was well known by parents and children in Enniskillen.

Parish priest Father Raymond Donnelly said: "Parents knew that their child was safe in the hands of Ellie."

Her body was found at a house in Enniskillen by police officers investigating a car crash.

They were called to the village of Tempo in County Fermanagh on Saturday 7 March where they found a car, but the driver had left the scene.

Officers then went to the house the car was registered to, where they discovered Ms Flanagan's body.

Martin McCarney, 45, from Enniskillen has been charged with her murder.

He told a court hearing he understood the charges against him and was remanded into custody.

Amy Doherty's family said she was the best mother to her two children and that her life revolved around her love and care of them.

The 28-year-old was found injured at a house in Summer Meadows Mews in Londonderry on 21 March and later died in hospital.

Her parents, Patrick and Sharon, said "her bubbly character and fun-loving spirit lifted the hearts of all who met her" and they have been "crushed with disbelief, sadness and pain".

A 30-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of murder and is being questioned by police.

This women and an eight-year-old girl were among three members of the same family found dead in what is being treated by police as a double murder and suicide.

The body of a 41-year-old man was also found at the house in Ballymena, County Antrim.

Details about their identity have not been released.

The PSNI has said it is not seeking anyone else in relation to the deaths.

articles.title: Idosa de 87 anos despejada na Espanha tem oferta para voltar para casa | G1
articles.standfirst: Governo espanhol aprovou nesta terça (29) medidas para tentar conter crise de habitação, incluindo proibição de despejos até 2030.
articles.summary: Governo espanhol aprovou nesta terça (29) medidas para tentar conter crise de habitação, incluindo proibição de despejos até 2030.
articles.body:
Maricarmen Abascal, idosa espanhola de 87 anos despejada do apartamento onde morava de aluguel, comparece a protesto popular em seu apoio em Madri, na Espanha, em 28 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: Reuters

A idosa espanhola Maricarmen Abascal, que foi despejada na semana passada do apartamento onde morava de aluguel havia sete décadas, recebeu uma oferta para voltar para casa, afirmou nesta terça-feira (29) sua advogada.

Beatriz Duro disse a jornalistas que a UrbaGestion, o fundo que é proprietário do apartamento onde Maricarmen morava, apresentou na noite de segunda-feira uma proposta preliminar de acordo que poderia permitir que a idosa de 87 anos voltasse para casa. Ela está considerando a oferta , acrescentou Duro.

Segundo Duro, o acordo implicaria pagar 30% de sua aposentadoria durante os próximos oito anos, o equivalente a cerca de € 500 por mês, um valor semelhante ao que ela pagava antes do despejo.

"Ela jamais deveria ter sido obrigada a sair", disse Duro. "Espero que este caso sirva para oferecer uma resposta coletiva à crise habitacional."

A movimentação ocorreu após dias de protestos em massa em Madri , capital espanhola, em repúdio ao despejo de Maricarmen.

Mesmo com a oferta na mão, a advogada de Maricarmen criticou a UrbaGestion por ter se recusado, até recentemente, a negociar ou manter conversas com a idosa. Ela também acusou as autoridades locais, regionais e nacionais de não responderem adequadamente ao problema habitacional da Espanha , especialmente aos despejos que deixam pessoas vulneráveis sem uma moradia alternativa.

Centenas de pessoas continuam acampadas nesta terça em uma das principais praças de Madri , a Puerta del Sol, para protestar contra o despejo de Maricarmen e exigindo reformas como o congelamento dos aluguéis e a renovação automática dos contratos sem aumentos abusivos.

Em resposta, o governo da Espanha aprovou nesta terça-feira novas medidas para conter a crise habitacional no país, incluindo uma proibição de despejos até 2030 , regras mais rígidas para aluguéis de curta duração e uma extensão de dois anos para contratos de aluguel já existentes.

"É hora de intervir no mercado imobiliário especulativo e começar a reequilibrar a balança entre os cidadãos e os fundos abutres", disse a ministra da Saúde espanhola, Monica Garcia.

O governo espanhol minoritário terá agora 30 dias a partir da publicação do decreto para chegar a um consenso com seus aliados no Congresso. As medidas serão votadas no Congresso na sexta-feira (2).

O Junts, partido catalão pró-independência que precisaria votar junto com o governo Sánchez para que o decreto fosse aprovado, disse concordar com a interrupção dos despejos abusivos, mas que ainda estava longe de estar de acordo com algumas medidas, como a proteção a pequenos proprietários.

Manifestantes em barracas na praça Puerta del Sol em Madri, na Espanha, protestam contra despejo de idosa de 87 anos em 28 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Juan Medina

articles.title: Boi invade loja de roupas em Timbaúba; VÍDEO | G1
articles.standfirst: Caso aconteceu em estabelecimento comercial localizado na área central de Timbaúba, município da Zona da Mata Norte de Pernambuco. Não houve feridos.
articles.summary: Vendedor de loja vizinha tentou laçar animal. Caso aconteceu em estabelecimento comercial localizado no Centro desse município da Zona da Mata Norte de Pernambuco.
articles.body:
Um boi invadiu uma loja de roupas no Centro de Timbaúba , na Zona da Mata Norte de Pernambuco, na tarde da segunda-feira (28). O animal foi filmado dentro do estabelecimento, na Rua Coronel Antônio Vicente, assustando lojistas e pessoas que passavam pelo local ( veja vídeo acima ). Não houve feridos.

Imagens do momento inusitado mostram um funcionário de outra loja tentando capturar e retirar o boi utilizando uma corda. O "boiadeiro" que aparece no vídeo é o vendedor Célio Andrade, que trabalha numa bomboniere vizinha ao estabelecimento invadido pelo animal.

Em entrevista ao g1 , Célio contou que tem experiência com animais rurais no sítio de parentes e disse que uma funcionária da loja de roupas ficou desesperada e pediu ajuda na rua.

"Entrou um boi assustado dentro do estabelecimento, o proprietário não estava. E assim, [a] menina estava do lado de fora, pedindo socorro, pedindo ajuda. A menina desesperada, porque não é todo dia que entra um boi dentro do estabelecimento. E então não tinha quem tirasse, aí eu me aventurei em tirar", disse o vendedor.

Outras pessoas aparecem nos vídeos tentando auxiliar, afastando o boi com bancos e outros objetos. Célio afirmou, ainda, que o proprietário da loja de roupas chegou depois e ajudou a laçar o animal para tirá-lo do estabelecimento.

Boi é filmado dentro de loja de roubas no município de Timbaúba — Foto: Montagem/g1

Ao sair da loja, o boi foi filmado circulando pelas ruas próximas à área comercial do município. Segundo Célio, o dono do animal apareceu depois e levou o boi embora. Mesmo com o susto, "ninguém se machucou, não quebrou muita coisa dentro da loja, também o boi não se feriu", contou o vendedor.

Procurada pelo g1 , a loja Vest Conforto disse que não gostaria de se pronunciar sobre o caso, mas informou que "todos estão bem". O g1 também entrou em contato com a prefeitura de Timbaúba para saber como é feita a fiscalização para evitar animais soltos nas ruas da cidade, mas não recebeu resposta até a última atualização desta reportagem.

articles.title: VÍDEO: Motociclistas são feridos por granizo durante supercélula no RS | G1
articles.standfirst: Grupo voltava de Manoel Viana em duas motocicletas quando foi surpreendido pelo temporal, a cerca de 5 km da chegada a Alegrete.
articles.summary: Motociclistas ficaram feridos após serem atingidos por granizo no RS durante a passagem de uma supercélula na BR-377, entre as cidades de Manoel Viana e Alegrete.
articles.body:
Dois casais que voltavam de um passeio em Manoel Viana para Alegrete , na Fronteira Oeste do Rio Grande do Sul, foram surpreendidos por chuva forte e granizo na BR-377, na noite de sábado (26). O grupo estava em duas motocicletas e ficou sem abrigo durante o temporal.

Segundo um dos motociclistas, Carlos Alberto, que registrou o momento, faltavam cerca de 5 km para a chegada quando as condições do tempo pioraram, por volta das 19h10. As quatro pessoas permaneceram no acostamento, expostas às pedras de gelo e ao vento.

Os quatro foram atingidos pelas pedras de gelo e ficaram com marcas e ferimentos pelo corpo . Ele registrou o momento e publicou nas redes sociais.

"A gente ficou na estrada, sem abrigo nenhum. Somente no cantinho do acostamento, segurando a moto e a esposa. Muito vento. Não tinha o que fazer, nem onde se abrigar", relatou.

⛈️ O grupo passou por uma supercélula, um tipo de tempestade severa caracterizada pela presença de uma corrente de ar ascendente que gira dentro da nuvem. Essa rotação, conhecida como mesociclone, faz com que a tempestade possa permanecer organizada e ativa por mais tempo do que uma tempestade comum. Esse tipo de formação pode provocar fenômenos extremos, como granizo de grandes dimensões, ventos muito fortes e, em determinadas condições, tornados.

A formação foi registrada durante uma sequência de temporais que atingiu o Rio Grande do Sul neste fim de semana. A Defesa Civil estadual havia emitido alerta para tempestades com possibilidade de granizo de grandes dimensões e rajadas de vento superiores a 80 km/h na tarde e noite de sábado. Para este domingo (27), a previsão indicava risco ainda maior, com ventos que poderiam superar 90 km/h.

Em Alegrete, o temporal provocou queda de granizo e danos em imóveis, especialmente na região de Passo Novo. Relatos locais apontaram casas destelhadas, alagamentos e problemas no fornecimento de energia elétrica

Conforme o motociclista, a base da polícia estadual mais próxima ficava cerca de 3 km à frente. Ele afirmou que a primeira queda de granizo durou aproximadamente três minutos.

"Deu uma pancada de uns três minutos e parou um pouquinho. Depois veio outra mais forte ainda", contou.

Ainda segundo o relato, o tempo mudou rapidamente. O motociclista afirmou que ainda estava claro antes do início do temporal e que o granizo representou o maior risco para o grupo.

"A chuva não era o problema, até porque é bom para lavar a alma. O problema foi o granizo", brincou.

articles.title: Ataque em escola na Eslováquia deixa morto e feridos | G1
articles.standfirst: Uma outra professora ficou ferida e uma aluna ficou em estado 'crítico', segundo autoridades locais. Adolescente de 13 anos foi detido.
articles.summary: Uma outra professora ficou ferida e uma aluna ficou em estado 'crítico', segundo autoridades locais. Adolescente de 13 anos foi detido.
articles.body:
Ataque em escola em Staškov, na Eslováquia, deixa morto e feridos em 29 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: Daniel Stehlik/TASR via AP

Um aluno matou uma professora e deixou outras duas pessoas feridas em um ataque com faca em uma escola na Eslováquia nesta terça-feira (29), segundo as autoridades locais.

O ataque ocorreu em Staškov, cidade com cerca de 3 mil habitantes no extremo norte do país.

"Esta manhã, após a primeira aula, um aluno cometeu um ataque com uma faca", afirmou o ministro do Interior, Matus Sutaj Estok.

Um adolescente de 13 anos que estuda na escola foi detido e está sendo investigado por assassinato , informou a polícia local.

A professora de 61 anos morreu no hospital em decorrência dos ferimentos, informaram os serviços de emergência à agência de notícias AFP.

Uma outra professora, de 44 anos, também foi hospitalizada após sofrer "uma facada no peito", mas não corre risco de vida. Uma aluna, que não teve sua idade revelada, está em estado "crítico" , informaram autoridades de saúde eslovacas.

O presidente da Eslováquia, Peter Pellegrini, afirmou estar "profundamente triste com o trágico incidente" e que "um ambiente de agressividade e intolerância impulsionado pelas redes sociais estão envenenando o espaço público".

O premiê Robert Fico enviou condolências à família da professora que morreu.

Em janeiro de 2025, um adolescente matou um colega de classe e uma professora e feriu outra pessoa em um ataque com faca em uma escola na cidade de Spisska Stara Ves, no nordeste da Eslováquia.

articles.title: Ônibus em Campinas: multas por atraso e ranking das piores linhas | G1
articles.standfirst: Levantamento da Emdec aponta que infrações superaram o total do ano passado em apenas oito meses. Passageiros reclamam de superlotação e perda de compromissos.
articles.summary: As multas por atraso de ônibus em Campinas somam R$ 15 milhões em 2026, com a linha 177 liderando o ranking de descumprimento de horários e viagens.
articles.body:
As multas aplicadas às empresas de ônibus por descumprimento de viagens em Campinas (SP) ultrapassaram a marca de R$ 15,6 milhões entre janeiro e agosto de 2026 . O valor já é maior do que todo o montante registrado no ano passado, e a linha 177 é a que apresenta o pior desempenho na cidade , segundo dados da Empresa Municipal de Desenvolvimento de Campinas (Emdec).

O balanço, obtido por meio da Lei de Acesso à Informação (LAI), mostra que a linha responsável por ligar os bairros DIC IV e V à região central, cumpriu apenas 68,47% das partidas previstas neste ano . O trajeto foi criado em outubro do ano passado para facilitar o deslocamento dos moradores, mas a falha na prestação do serviço afeta diretamente a rotina dos passageiros.

Além da 177, outras rotas da cidade também apresentam altos índices de viagens não realizadas. Veja as cinco linhas que menos cumpriram o cronograma em 2026:

1º lugar — Linha 177: 68,47% de cumprimento

2º lugar — Linha 389: 75,10% de cumprimento

3º lugar — Linha BRT26: 78,63% de cumprimento

4º lugar — Linha 416: 79,06% de cumprimento

5º lugar — Linha 390: 81,66% de cumprimento

A faxineira Josiane Onório, que utiliza o transporte diariamente, relata os transtornos causados pela espera da 177. "Às vezes você fica ali no ponto e ela não vem. Aí você tem que pegar o outro lotado. A gente paga bem caro para isso e acaba não tendo", afirma.

A incerteza sobre os horários faz com que os moradores busquem alternativas para não perderem compromissos. "Teve vezes de eu pegar outro ônibus porque ele não passou. A gente fica refém desses horários que eles não cumprem", conta a assistente administrativo Eclésia de Cássia.

Ônibus da linha 177 do transporte público municipal de Campinas — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

O número de infrações registradas pela Emdec saltou de 10.544, em 2024, para 30.769 apenas até a metade de agosto de 2026. Confira a evolução dos valores aplicados em penalidades pelo não cumprimento de viagens:

2026 (até 16 de agosto): R$ 15.690.959,24

O intervalo previsto entre os veículos da linha 177 deveria ser de 21 minutos, mas a demora gera superlotação nos horários de pico. "A partir das seis, dez para seis, ninguém entra. Todo mundo estressado por causa das linhas, não passa, quando passa ali não para", relata a empregada doméstica Márcia Reis.

A Emdec informou em nota que os índices operacionais da maioria das linhas que fazem parte do ranking são impactados pelo trajeto e circulação por trechos de rodovia, que apresentam períodos de lentidão nos horários de pico, como é o caso da linha 177 e a 416.

Disse ainda que a operação da 177 vem sendo impactada pela falta de veículo, situação que também vem ocorrendo nas linhas BRT25 e BRT26 e que gera multas aos operadores. A fiscalização nas linhas segue sendo feita em pontos de parada, garagens e terminais.

Ainda segundo a Emdec, entre os pontos previstos na nova concessão do transporte coletivo está a reorganização de trajetos e programação de parte das linhas a partir desses índices.

Depois de dar essas explicações, a Emdec acrescentou que de maneira geral o sistema de transporte coletivo como um todo cumpre 92% das partidas

O sindicato das empresas de transporte de passageiros da região metropolitana de Campinas, que representa a empresa VB, informou que a linha 177, opera com quatro veículos.

No entanto, diz que um deles foi vandalizado na segunda-feira (28) e, por esse motivo, não pôde circular nesta terça (29), o que reduziu a oferta desta linha.

Os demais veículos operaram normalmente. Além da linha 177, a região também conta com atendimento das linhas 114, 115 e 117.

articles.title: Prédio do Adolfo Lutz em Sorocaba está deteriorado e abandonado | G1
articles.standfirst: Imóvel é usado pela Secretaria de Estado da Saúde e apresenta mofo, vidros quebrados e mato alto. Estado diz que reforma está em fase de avaliação.
articles.summary: O prédio da Secretaria de Estado da Saúde (SES), onde funciona o Instituto Adolfo Lutz (IAL), no Centro de Sorocaba (SP), está em estado de abandono.
articles.body:
O prédio da Secretaria de Estado da Saúde (SES), onde funciona o Instituto Adolfo Lutz (IAL), no Centro de Sorocaba (SP), está em estado de abandono. O local abrigava o Palácio da Saúde, hoje administrado pelo município em outro endereço.

Nos últimos dias, a TV TEM recebeu várias fotos de pessoas que trabalham no entorno e que ficaram incomodadas com a situação de abandono do prédio. Pessoas reclamam que a situação faz com que animais peçonhentos apareçam nos prédios do bairro.

Entre moradores e até funcionários do Estado, o local é apelidado de "prédio abandonado" . A arquitetura apresenta sinais de deterioração em praticamente todos os pontos e ângulos.

De palácio da saúde a símbolo do abandono: prédio do Adolfo Lutz se deteriora no Centro de Sorocaba (SP) — Foto: Marcel Scinocca/g1

É possível identificar bolor, pintura descascada e vidros danificados. No estacionamento, há veículos usados em serviços oficiais que também estão abandonados.

O prédio tem três pavimentos, mais de 60 anos e ocupa quase um quarteirão inteiro entre a Rua Júlio Hanser e a Avenida Comendador Pereira Inácio. Na fachada, os sinais de abandono são evidentes e mostram o estado de conservação do imóvel.

Há mato alto, falta de manutenção das plantas, lixo acumulado e restos de vegetação nas três passarelas que dão acesso à parte principal do prédio. Todos os acessos estão permanentemente fechados.

O avanço da deterioração também pode ser verificado por meio do Google Street View. A primeira imagem foi registrada em 2011. Na época, o prédio não estava em condições perfeitas, mas apresentava características muito diferentes da situação atual. A piora aparece ao longo dos registros fotográficos feitos em 2019, 2023 e 2025.

A Secretaria de Estado da Saúde informou ao g1 que o projeto de reforma do imóvel está em fase de avaliação pela pasta, mas não informou o prazo para a conclusão da reforma nem quando o local foi revitalizado pela última vez.

"O projeto prevê que, após a reforma, o prédio passe a abrigar as unidades regionais de Vigilância em Saúde e o Departamento Regional de Saúde (DRS) de Sorocaba", disse a Secretaria, em nota.

À TV TEM , a secretaria acrescentou que os serviços de manutenção e zeladoria têm sido feitos por uma empresa terceirizada. Nesta terça-feira (29), constatou-se o início do processo de manutenção do local.

articles.title: Sesi oferece 90 bolsas para Ensino Médio e técnico no Agreste | G1
articles.standfirst: São 45 vagas para Ensino Médio integrado ao curso de Administração em Caruaru e 45 para Ensino Médio integrado ao curso de Desenvolvimento de Sistemas em Belo Jardim.
articles.summary: Sesi abre edital de bolsas de estudo gratuitas para cursos técnicos integrados ao ensino médio em Caruaru e Belo Jardim.
articles.body:
Sesi-PE abre edital de vagas de bolsas de estudo no interior de Pernambuco — Foto: Divulgação

O Serviço Social da Indústria de Pernambuco (Sesi-PE) abriu 90 bolsas de estudos gratuitas para o Ensino Médio integrado à formação técnica em 2027, no Agreste de Pernambuco. Em Caruaru , são 45 vagas para o curso de Administração e, em Belo Jardim , outras 45 para Desenvolvimento de Sistemas. As inscrições começam nesta terça-feira (29) e seguem até 5 de outubro, na internet .

Em Caruaru, as oportunidades são para Administração, integrado ao Ensino Médio, no turno da tarde. Já em Belo Jardim, as vagas são para Desenvolvimento de Sistemas, também no período vespertino. A seleção é destinada a estudantes que estejam cursando o 9º ano do Ensino Fundamental ou que já tenham concluído essa etapa.

Para participar, o estudante precisa ter, no máximo, 16 anos completos até 31 de dezembro de 2027. Como os candidatos são menores de idade, a inscrição deve ser realizada pelo responsável legal.

As vagas gratuitas são destinadas ao público em geral, desde que seja apresentada autodeclaração de baixa renda no momento da matrícula. Do total de vagas de cada unidade, 60% são destinadas a dependentes de trabalhadores da indústria pernambucana, Microempreendedores Individuais (MEIs) enquadrados na categoria da indústria ou empregados das instituições que integram o Sistema FIEPE.

Os outros 40% das vagas são destinados à ampla concorrência. A inscrição é gratuita e deve ser feita exclusivamente pela internet, no site da banca organizadora , onde também está disponível o edital .

A seleção será realizada em uma única etapa, com uma prova objetiva presencial, de caráter eliminatório e classificatório. A avaliação terá 40 questões de múltipla escolha, sendo 20 de Língua Portuguesa e 20 de Matemática.

No Sesi Caruaru, são 45 vagas para Administração, no turno vespertino. A unidade fica na Rua Maria Eliete, nº 437, no bairro Maria Auxiliadora.

No Sesi Belo Jardim, são 45 vagas para Desenvolvimento de Sistemas, também no turno vespertino. A unidade fica na Rua Coronel Antônio Marinho, nº 120, no bairro Boa Vista.

As inscrições ficam abertas de 29 de setembro a 5 de outubro de 2026.

O cartão com o local de prova será divulgado em 22 de outubro.

A prova está marcada para 1º de novembro.

O gabarito definitivo e o resultado dos recursos serão divulgados em 9 de novembro.

O resultado definitivo dos classificados está previsto para 26 de novembro.

A matrícula presencial dos aprovados será realizada entre 30 de novembro e 3 de dezembro de 2026.

articles.title: Jornalista vira rei em Uganda em meio a disputa por sucessão | G1
articles.standfirst: Coroação ocorre um mês após a morte de Oyo Nyimba, que ficou conhecido mundialmente por ter sido coroado aos 3 anos.
articles.summary: Coroação ocorre um mês após a morte de Oyo Nyimba, que ficou conhecido mundialmente por ter sido coroado aos 3 anos.
articles.body:
O futuro rei de Tooro, Edward Rukidi Nyabongo I, realiza rituais e cerimônias tradicionais antes de sua coroação. — Foto: Abubaker Lubowa / Reuters

Um jornalista deve ser coroado nesta terça-feira (29) como rei de uma monarquia tradicional que perdeu seu antigo “rei menino” no mês passado, desencadeando uma onda de luto e uma disputa sucessória no Reino de Tooro, em Uganda.

O jornalista é um príncipe qu e trabalhou por muitos anos como apresentador e editor da Uganda Broadcasting Corp. Ele adotou o nome real de Edward Rukidi Nyabongo. Após participar de rituais durante a noite, foi conduzido ao palácio e será oficialmente apresentado a seus súditos ainda nesta terça-feira.

Os reinos tradicionais foram proibidos na década de 1960, após a independência de Uganda do domínio colonial britânico, por um presidente republicano que dizia querer unificar o país. Eles foram restaurados em 1993.

Os líderes tradicionais não exercem autoridade formal nesse país da África Oriental e são legalmente proibidos de participar da política partidária. Ainda assim, exercem grande influência entre suas populações como guardiões da cultura tradicional.

A cerimônia de coroação em Fort Portal, uma cidade remota no oeste de Uganda, próxima à fronteira com a República Democrática do Congo, será acompanhada por milhares de pessoas presencialmente e pela televisão.

Em entrevista ao jornal local New Vision antes da coroação, Nyabongo prometeu promover a unidade e afirmou que “a herança deve vir acompanhada de disciplina e trabalho duro. Minha família nunca me permitiu tratar a ascendência real como um privilégio; ela sempre me foi apresentada como um dever para o qual eu deveria me preparar”.

Ele não estava entre os primeiros na linha sucessória, mas foi escolhido pelos anciãos do clã governante do reino, conhecido como Babiito, entre um grupo de príncipes elegíveis após a morte do rei Oyo Nyimba, vítima de câncer aos 34 anos em agosto, sem deixar um herdeiro publicamente conhecido.

Retrato do rei Oyo Nyimba exibido dentro da Catedral de São João, em Fort Portal, Uganda, perto da fronteira com o Congo. — Foto: Patrick Onen / AP

A rainha-mãe, Best Kemigisa, contestou a decisão e afirmou que o testamento deixado por Oyo não foi respeitado na escolha de Nyabongo.

Kemigisa disse que Oyo deixou um filho pequeno, cuja identidade seria revelada no momento apropriado, lançando dúvidas sobre a legitimidade de Nyabongo e da decisão tomada pelos Babiito. A imprensa local relatou cenas de desentendimento, incluindo uma breve disputa pela custódia dos restos mortais do rei, durante o funeral de Oyo em 12 de setembro.

Embora o suposto filho de Oyo ainda não tenha sido apresentado publicamente, supostas fotos de um “Baby Oyo” inundaram as redes sociais e alimentaram a esperança dos admiradores do monarca falecido. Críticos, porém, afirmam que a criança, caso exista, deveria ter sido apresentada aos anciãos do reino enquanto o pai ainda estava vivo.

“Eles demonstraram que essas são as normas do reino”, afirmou Nicholas Sengoba, um conhecido analista político de Uganda, referindo-se à escolha de Nyabongo pelos Babiito. “Muitas dessas decisões podem não ser populares.”

Oyo foi coroado em 1995, aos 3 anos de idade, após a morte do pai. Tornou-se uma figura curiosa, vestida com trajes coloridos, e objeto de admiração para centenas de milhares de súditos.

Durante sua coroação, participou de uma série de rituais tribais e foi levado ao cemitério real para realizar uma cerimônia de passagem para a vida adulta: lançar com sucesso nove grãos de café sobre o túmulo de seu pai.

Pessoas reunidas para o funeral do rei Oyo Nyimba, de Tooro. — Foto: Patrick Onen / AP

Oyo chegou a deter informalmente o título de rei mais jovem do mundo e era uma figura fascinante até mesmo para líderes mundiais apresentados a ele em eventos oficiais, entre eles Nelson Mandela, da África do Sul.

O líder líbio Muammar Gaddafi esteve entre aqueles que cultivaram uma relação próxima com a família real de Tooro, tratando-a como parte de sua família ampliada. Gaddafi visitou Uganda diversas vezes e apoiou Oyo e Kemigisa por anos, até sua morte, em outubro de 2011.

Oyo foi orientado por regentes nomeados pelo reino até atingir a maioridade, aos 18 anos.

articles.title: Homem apontado como elo entre TCP e milícia é preso após operação | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo o Ministério Público, Thauan da Silva Menezes atuava na articulação entre traficantes da facção e grupos paramilitares da Zona Oeste. Prisão ocorreu horas após ação que terminou com três mortos e 13 feridos.
articles.summary: A Polícia Militar prendeu, no fim da noite de segunda-feira (28), um dos alvos da operação realizada no Complexo da Maré, na Zona Norte do Rio.
articles.body:
A Polícia Militar prendeu, no fim da noite de segunda-feira (28), um dos alvos da operação realizada no Complexo da Maré, na Zona Norte do Rio, que terminou com três mortos e 13 feridos. Segundo a corporação, Thauan da Silva Menezes foi abordado na Linha Amarela enquanto tentava fugir da região.

De acordo com o Ministério Público do Estado do Rio de Janeiro (MPRJ), Thauan fazia a ligação entre integrantes do Terceiro Comando Puro (TCP) e grupos milicianos na disputa contra traficantes do Comando Vermelho (CV).

Ele foi interceptado por agentes do Batalhão de Rondas Especiais e Controle de Multidões (Recom) na saída da Vila do João. Segundo a PM, Thauan estava na garupa de uma motocicleta e se preparava para deixar a comunidade.

Thauan foi preso no fim da noite de segunda-feira (28) — Foto: Reprodução

Ainda de acordo com a polícia, havia contra ele um mandado de prisão por associação para o tráfico de drogas.

As investigações do MPRJ apontam que Thauan integra o TCP e atua na Vila do João, onde seria responsável pela venda de drogas e armas. O órgão afirma que ele era um dos principais articuladores da aliança entre a facção e a milícia da Zona Oeste da cidade, criada para expandir o controle territorial sobre áreas dominadas pelo CV.

A prisão ocorreu poucas horas após a operação da PM no Complexo da Maré, cujo objetivo era combater a atuação de integrantes do TCP e reduzir a circulação de armas na comunidade.

Ônibus escolar é usado como barricada na Linha Vermelha — Foto: Allan Cavalcante / TV Globo

O traficante Álvaro Malaquias Santa Rosa, conhecido como Peixão e apontado como um dos chefes do TCP, também é alvo de investigações. A Polícia Civil apura se ele ordenou a interceptação de dois ônibus na Linha Vermelha, na altura de Duque de Caxias, na Baixada Fluminense, em represália à operação.

Segundo a investigação, a ação teria como objetivo desviar agentes que participavam da operação para outra região.

Em um dos ônibus estavam estudantes de um colégio particular da Barra da Tijuca, que seguiam para uma excursão em Vassouras, no Sul Fluminense.

A Linha Vermelha ficou interditada por cerca de uma hora. Ninguém ficou ferido.

Ao final da operação, a PM informou ter apreendido 12 fuzis, oito pistolas, granadas, 83 quilos de drogas e seis veículos roubados.

articles.title: Executivo do New York Times é morto a tiros; sogros são suspeitos | G1
articles.standfirst: Documentos judiciais revelados pelo próprio New York Times registram disputas e acusações de violência entre McKinsey e sua esposa
articles.summary: Documentos judiciais revelados pelo próprio New York Times registram disputas e acusações de violência entre McKinsey e sua esposa
articles.body:
Documentos judiciais revelados pelo próprio New York Times registram disputas e acusações de violência entre McKinsey e sua esposa. — Foto: Reprodução/LinkedIn via BBC

Um executivo do jornal americano The New York Times foi morto a tiros na Califórnia, supostamente pelos pais de sua esposa, que foram presos por suspeita de homicídio.

Jonathan McKinsey, de 40 anos, diretor do setor de engenharia de jogos do jornal, foi encontrado morto na tarde de sábado (26/09) com vários ferimentos a bala em um estacionamento em Dublin, a 56 km de São Francisco, segundo informou a polícia.

Seus sogros, Shouyong Zhang e Shili Chen, ambos de 77 anos, foram presos em conexão com o caso e enfrentam várias acusações, incluindo homicídio em primeiro grau.

Eles devem comparecer ao tribunal nesta quarta-feira (30/09) para uma audiência de instrução.

O The New York Times confirmou a morte de McKinsey.

Testemunhas disseram à emissora KGO-TV terem ouvido uma rajada de tiros antes de encontrarem a vítima morta.

"Eu vi o homem cair no chão, com a cabeça e o peito cobertos de sangue", disse Assad Razawi à emissora local.

A filha de Razawi acrescentou que o pai viu o casal de idosos "caminhando juntos e depois se afastando calmamente do local do tiroteio".

Shouyong Zhang e Shili Chen foram presos minutos depois por um policial que passava pelo local. Segundo outra testemunha, o casal permaneceu na área após o incidente.

McKinsey foi declarado morto no local. A polícia não revelou o motivo do assassinato.

O casal de idosos está detido na Cadeia do Condado de Santa Rita, na Califórnia.

Eles também enfrentam acusações de conspiração para cometer crimes, disparo intencional de arma de fogo por negligência grave e ações que colocaram crianças em perigo.

Segundo o New York Times, documentos judiciais do Condado de Alameda mostram que a esposa de McKinsey, Candice Jang, entrou com um pedido de medida protetiva alegando violência doméstica em outubro de 2025.

Ela também solicitou uma ordem de proteção contra o executivo para seus três filhos e sua mãe.

Em dezembro passado, McKinsey entrou com um pedido de medida protetiva contra sua esposa , alegando violência doméstica. Ele também havia apresentado um pedido de divórcio.

articles.title: Escolas do AM suspendem aulas presenciais por problemas estruturais | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo estudantes e pais de alunos, as unidades enfrentam problemas estruturais, principalmente no sistema elétrico.
articles.summary: Escolas estaduais do Amazonas em Maués interrompem atividades presenciais devido a falhas elétricas, prejudicando estudantes com acesso limitado à internet.
articles.body:
Aulas presenciais são suspensas em escolas estaduais de Maués após problemas estruturais — Foto: Reprodução/Rede Amazônica

As aulas presenciais foram suspensas em pelo menos duas escolas estaduais de Maués , no interior do Amazonas, desde a última semana. Segundo estudantes e pais de alunos, as unidades enfrentam problemas estruturais, principalmente no sistema elétrico.

Uma das escolas afetadas é a Escola Estadual São Pedro, que tem cerca de mil alunos matriculados. As atividades presenciais foram interrompidas no dia 23 de setembro e, desde então, os estudantes estão acompanhando as aulas de forma remota.

A mudança preocupa pais de alunos que relatam dificuldades para acompanhar as atividades a distância. A situação é ainda mais complicada para estudantes que vivem na zona rural e em comunidades ribeirinhas, onde o acesso à internet pode ser limitado.

Rangel Nascimento, pai de um aluno da Escola São Pedro, disse que a família consegue acompanhar as atividades, mas que nem todos os estudantes têm a mesma estrutura.

"Agora nós, como pais, ficamos preocupados com a comunidade, porque tem alunos que são da zona rural. São ribeirinhos e eles não têm muitas vezes acesso à internet de forma rápida que nós temos na cidade."

Além da Escola São Pedro, a Escola Estadual Professora Maria das Graças Nogueira também está com as aulas presenciais suspensas. Segundo relatos da comunidade escolar, a unidade enfrenta problemas semelhantes.

A falta de informações sobre quando as atividades presenciais serão retomadas também preocupa os pais.

A Secretaria de Estado de Educação e Desporto Escolar (Seduc) foi procurada para saber quais problemas foram identificados nas escolas, quais medidas estão sendo adotadas e quando as aulas presenciais devem ser retomadas, mas até a última atualização desta reportagem, não houve retorno.

articles.title: Ônibus e ferry: Transportes da Bahia serão gratuitos nas Eleições 2026 | G1
articles.standfirst: Governo da Bahia emitiu decretos que tornam metrô, ônibus intermunicipais, lanchinhas e ferry boat gratuitos no domingo (4).
articles.summary: Governo da Bahia emitiu decretos que tornam metrô, ônibus intermunicipais, lanchinhas e ferry boat gratuitos no domingo (4).
articles.body:
Ferry-boat Ivete Sangalo — Foto: Internacional Travessias Salvador (ITS)

Os transportes intermunicipais serão gratuitos no domingo (4), dia do 1º turno das Eleições 2026, e em 25 de outubro, caso haja 2º turno. A informação foi publicada nesta terça-feira (29), no Diário Oficial do Estado.

A gratuidade comporta os ônibus intermunicipais, o ferry boat e as lanchinhas. Anteriormente, a prefeitura da capital baiana e a CCR Metrô, operadora responsável pelo metrô de Salvador , já tinham divulgado as gratuidades das passagens no 1º turno.

Nesta reportagem, o g1 detalhou como vai funcionar a gratuidade nos diferentes sistemas.

De acordo com o Decreto nº 24.833, a partir das 18h de sábado (3) até as 23:59h de domingo (4), a utilização do serviço público de transporte coletivo intermunicipal rodoviário será gratuita.

Caso haja segundo turno, a gratuidade será valida entre as 18h do dia 24 de outubro até as 23:59h do dia 25 de outubro.

Para não pagar a passagem, os eleitores deverão apresentar o título de eleitor que comprove o local de votação e o documento de identidade.

O Decreto nº 24.834 faz referência ao metrô, ferry boat, lanchinhas e no transporte metropolitano do Estado da Bahia.

A utilização gratuita do serviço de ferry boat é prevista apenas aos pedestres. Ou seja, quem usar o sistema com veículos vai precisar pagar a tarifa.

No decreto, não há informações sobre a necessidade de precisar comprovar o local de votação através do título de eleitor.

articles.title: Lindsay Clancy's push to probe holdout juror hits snag before pivotal retrial hearing
articles.summary: Lindsay Clancy returns to court in person as her defense pushes a double jeopardy motion and seeks to investigate holdout juror Michael Desronvil.
articles.body:
Massachusetts judge to hear arguments on Lindsay Clancy's double jeopardy motion, while push to investigate lone holdout juror may be on hold.

Clancy expected in court for first time since mistrial, with national interest in case remaining high.

Defense attorney calls for inquiry into holdout juror, who opposed 11 others on panel, as prosecutors and defense agree to adjourn motion.

PLYMOUTH, Mass. — A Massachusetts judge overseeing the Lindsay Clancy case is expected to hear arguments on her double jeopardy motion Tuesday, while another push to investigate the lone holdout juror in her mistrial may be on hold — for now.

Clancy is expected in court in person for the first time since her trial ended in a deadlocked jury and the judge declared a mistrial on Sept. 4.

In the weeks since her mistrial, Clancy's case has remained a topic of national interest, with fellow jurors and Clancy's defense attorney attacking the lone holdout. At the same time, Plymouth County District Attorney Tim Cruz's office has been relatively quiet about their plans for a potential retrial.

Here's a roundup of what to expect as she returns to court:

Clancy's defense lawyer Kevin Reddington had called for an inquiry into the lone holdout juror, Michael Desronvil, whom he has dubbed "the obstructionist juror." Desronvil opposed 11 others on the panel and was the only one who wanted to find her guilty until the end.

Michael Desronvil, who is said to be hiding out at an undisclosed location, spoke out publicly for the first time in a video exclusively shared with Fox News' "Hannity" Monday evening.

"I know the whole focus has been on me, but we want to reel everything back and put the focus on the three angels," he said. "The ones that can't speak for themselves, the ones that can't defend themselves, and the ones that can't fight the battles — and those are Cora, Dawson and Callan."

According to Desronvil's attorney, Edward Paltzik, both Reddington and Plymouth County prosecutors agreed to adjourn that motion after counsel for the holdout raised an objection because they didn't yet have access to impounded materials necessary to file a response.

"The DA and Reddington consent to adjourn the motion to investigate Michael," Paltzik told Fox News' Kayleigh McEnany Monday.

"If Judge Sullivan signs an order today, much of it could be adjourned," he said. "Either way, a status conference is still likely."

Reddington pushed back, forcefully, while conceding that he and the district attorney's office had agreed to continue the motion out of professional courtesy to local counsel now representing the juror.

"Earlier today, both the government and I were contacted by a professional local attorney who represents Juror Doe," he said, not using the juror's name due to an impoundment order from the court. "That attorney requested — as any qualified counsel would — adequate time to review our motion and reply."

He added, "As is professional courtesy, both the government and I agreed to continue this specific motion to a later date at their request. The motion remains active, fully alive, and is currently pending a ruling from Judge Sullivan. We will not allow a publicity-seeking opportunist to twist simple courtroom courtesy into a victory that does not exist."

The terms adjourned and continued are similar but have distinct meanings.

"Adjournment generally signifies that something like a hearing is off indefinitely especially because no date is specified," explained retired Massachusetts Judge Carol Erskine. "A continuance is a simple request by a party or two parties to get a new date. [Reddington] objects because adjournment is a misrepresentation of what is happening."

If Reddington ultimately prevails, the court could hold a Fidler hearing , where the judge would question Desronvil.

"There are three phases to a hearing like that," said Erskine, who is also a child welfare advocate and has been closely following the case. "This is something that could result in a strong manifest necessity claim but hard to tell until it happens."

Manifest necessity is the legal standard required to hold a second trial . Erskine said the motion is a long-shot but Reddington is likely laying the foundation for an appeal in the future.

"The big issue, in my opinion, is whether outside information came into the jury room and whether a judge can find that any 'hypothetical juror' would let it influence his decision," she told Fox News Digital. "It's definitely more complicated than that, but there is case law about it."

"This is a strange new world in which disagreeing jurors and their surrogates conduct a public debate after the trial in the media and social media," said Jack Lu, another retired Massachusetts judge.

Reddington's request for an inquiry into Desronvil is largely based on allegations from other jurors who accused him of having reasonable doubt about the case and ignoring it. He is seeking phone records, his confidential juror questionnaire and police records.

However, he's also called him an "obstructionist" outside the courtroom and accused him of having an "agenda."

"[The other jurors] know that they were robbed — by one man — for whatever his agenda was, who stole seven weeks of the life of these other jurors that were so attentive, so beautiful, so wonderful and listened to this evidence," he told reporters after leaving the courthouse on Sept. 4, the day the mistrial was declared.

Still, he downplayed speculation from legal analysts about a potential defamation lawsuit from the holdout against Clancy's team.

"Defamation law is textbook complex," he told Fox News Digital. "Statements made in court proceedings are privileged."

Statements made out of court that could appear to be "false statements of fact" may end up being considered opinions, he added.

"If a person says X happened, and we all know that person was not present, then it may be deemed to be an opinion," he said. "This might apply to any alleged statements about what happened in the jury room."

"I don't think any of the legal maneuvering, double jeopardy, all that stuff, a hearing in the trial court with the juror, I don't think it's going anywhere," said Mark Bederow, a New York-based criminal defense attorney and former prosecutor who is following the case.

"If you get down to brass tacks, once you get through all this, now you have to look at the DA and say, what are you doing?" he added.

Most prosecutors would not seek a second trial in a case where only one juror agreed with them, he said, but that appears unlikely in this case.

"At the first trial, the prosecution, in my view, failed miserably to satisfy their burden — but there is a credible argument that she's guilty and intended to cause their deaths and knew right from wrong," he said. "In order for them to win, they need to get better experts."

The Commonwealth needs experts who can discredit Clancy's defense experts, he said. And prosecutors also have room to improve their jury selection.

As for Reddington, he described him as "a titan of the Massachusetts bar" who is filing motions that make sense for his client's benefit, regardless of his commentary outside the courtroom.

"That's not frivolous, and any lawyer knows that," he told Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Pentagon awards RTX's Raytheon $20.7 billion AMRAAM contract amid stockpile concerns
articles.summary: The Pentagon has moved to rapidly expand production of one of the US military's key air-to-air missiles, awarding RTX's Raytheon business a provisional
articles.body: The Pentagon has moved to rapidly expand production of one of the US military's key air-to-air missiles, awarding RTX's Raytheon business a provisional multiyear contract worth $20.7 billion for AMRAAM missiles.The move comes as the US seeks to rebuild weapons stocks that have been drawn down by conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine. Washington has supplied large quantities of weapons to its allies while also using munitions during its own military operations in Iran, putting additional pressure on inventories of air defence and precision-guided weapons.The AMRAAM is used by fighter aircraft to engage enemy planes and is also deployed in NASAMS, a ground-based air defence system used to protect the Washington area. More than a dozen countries, including Ukraine, Oman and Qatar, also operate NASAMS.The proposed deal is part of a wider Pentagon effort this year to persuade defence contractors to increase weapons production more quickly. A similar approach was used for a $58.6 billion Patriot interceptor contract awarded to Lockheed Martin in July, covering procurement through fiscal 2032.However, the full value of the AMRAAM commitment still depends on Congress providing the required funding. Defence industry executives have warned that without those appropriations, contractors may not be able to make large-scale investments in factories, equipment and components.The production deals are part of the Trump administration's broader push to expand US weapons manufacturing and prioritise military production over shareholder returns. If Congress provides the funding, the RTX contract would allow the company to expand its workforce, supply chain and manufacturing capacity as demand from the US military rises.RTX said it had nearly doubled AMRAAM production in 2025 from the previous year. The deal would fall under the Pentagon's "Arsenal of Freedom" initiative, while RTX has set a target of producing at least 1,900 AMRAAM missiles each year.

articles.title: Scrapping pensions triple lock 'morally wrong', says union boss
articles.summary: Andy Burnham wants to outline his ideas for a free-at-the-point-of-use social care system in his first speech to Labour conference as prime minister.
articles.body:
Unite the Union general secretary Sharon Graham has warned the prime minister that scrapping the pensions triple lock would be "morally wrong", as Andy Burnham prepares to deliver his first speech to Labour conference as PM.

Burnham told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg that he wants to use his speech to set out his "vision" to introduce an NHS-style social care system, free at the point of use.

There is growing speculation about how such a care system could be funded, including removing the pensions triple lock in the future.

Labour's deputy leader Lucy Powell told BBC Breakfast the party is committed to the triple lock, which was in the party's 2024 manifesto.

The triple lock, which has been in place for 16 years, means state pensions rise every April by at least 2.5% or in line with the highest of prices or earnings.

Speaking to BBC Radio 4's Today programme, Graham said axing the triple lock risked repeating the unpopular removal of the Winter Fuel Allowance under previous prime minister Sir Keir Starmer.

"Instead of going to try and pick the pocket of pensioners, we need to move over to the other side of the equation and think about things like wealth taxes way before we try to stop something like the triple lock," she said.

"Going to a group of people who are getting around £12,500 a year in order to pay for it [social care], to take away their security, is wrong - I think its morally wrong," she added, highlighting how current pensions are the lowest of the G7 countries.

On Tuesday morning, Powell said the lock was a manifesto commitment, and asked whether it would stay in place until the next election, she said: "I can absolutely assure your viewers watching this that we are committed to the triple lock, it's in our manifesto.

"The triple lock is really delivering for pensioners right now: over the course of this parliament it's set to increase the value of the state pension by around about £2,000 a year - significant uplifts to the state pension."

Speaking to the BBC, Burnham set out his proposal for a new social care system to help people live more independently. He said social care in England is "as unfair as American healthcare, where the most vulnerable in society can lose everything, they can be wiped out" and indicated "nothing is off the table at this moment in time" on funding.

Unlike the NHS, social care is not free at the point of use. In England and Northern Ireland, people with savings worth more than £23,250 are not entitled to help with care costs from their council.

In Wales and Scotland, different rules apply in terms of eligibility.

Alan Milburn, the former Labour minister who is currently leading an independent review into young people and work for the government, has said scrapping the triple lock to fund social care is "the sort of call" the prime minister is "prepared to make".

In the BBC's Political Thinking podcast, Milburn was asked if Burnham's new social care plans could be funded by getting rid of the triple lock, he responded that Burnham was "exactly the sort of person who can take the big decisions".

He said: "Andy is absolutely right about this - the social care system is broken... That is going to be a really big call.

"But it's the sort of call that I've got no doubt - from everything, and every conversation I've been in with him - it's the sort of call that he is prepared to make."

Burnham is also expected to announce a new government body to invest in Britain's electricity grid, branded Great British Grid , in his speech.

articles.title: The night India hit back after Uri attack: 10 years since the surgical strikes set a new template
articles.summary: India today marks ten years since the surgical strikes of September 29, 2016, an operation that came to define a new template for the country's
articles.body: India today marks ten years since the surgical strikes of September 29, 2016, an operation that came to define a new template for the country's counter-terrorism response and set the stage for the bolder military actions that followed in the decade since.The strikes were carried out in direct retaliation for the Uri attack of September 18, 2016, when terrorists belonging to Jaish-e-Mohammed struck the Army's brigade headquarters located in Uri in Jammu and Kashmir. The terror attack claimed the lives of 19 soldiers, who belonged to the 10th battalion of the Dogra Regiment and the 6th battalion of the Bihar Regiment.A fire caused by the combat spread through the camp's tents and barracks and is believed to be the reason for the toll climbing this high. This was not the first terror attack in that sector. Terrorists had attacked the Mohura camp in Uri less than two years earlier, in December 2014, which had claimed the lives of 11 security personnel and six terrorists. 2016 also saw the terror attack at the Pathankot air base, which had come just days after PM Modi's impromptu visit to Pakistan.The night India crossed the LoCThe response to the terror attack came less than two weeks later. On the intervening night of September 28 and 29, paratroopers of the Army's elite Para Special Forces (SF) units crossed the Line of Control in the wee hours and entered Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, striking seven terror launch pads across the Bhimber, Hotspring, Kel and Lipa sectors.The targets were located two to three kilometres from the LoC and had reportedly been under surveillance for over a week. The elite SF operatives penetrated between 500 metres and two kilometres into Pakistani-held territory during the nearly five-hour operation, which wound down by around 4.30 am as the raiders withdrew to the safety of the Indian side. Intelligence estimates placed casualties between 35 and 70 terrorists killed.2016 started with the terror attack on the Pathankot air base, there were a series of incidents through the year including the one at the EDI building. We wanted to hit back and after Uri, the then defence minister Late Manohar Parrikar cleared my proposal to take the fight to the enemy. The attack caused heavy damage to the terrorists, while we weren't harmed by enemy fire at all. The attack also proved that India will strike back across the border and proved our resolve. The strikes paved the way for operations like Balakot Air strike and Op Sindoor later, to protect India from terrorists anywhere. The strikes paved the way for operations like Balakot Air strike and Op Sindoor later, to protect India from terrorists anywhere.What made the surgical strikes differentWhat made the operation stand apart from previous cross-LoC raids, which have historically been conducted quietly at the battalion, brigade or divisional level, was that this series of strikes was novel in scale and in the political decision to publicly own it.The planning involved the Prime Minister's Office and the then Army chief, while the government had given the Army a free hand to plan and execute the response. The strikes also inspired the 2019 Bollywood film *Uri: The Surgical Strike*.From Uri to Balakot and Operation SindoorA decade on, the 2016 surgical strikes are widely seen as the moment India's counter-terrorism posture shifted from restraint to visible retaliation. The template set that September, striking terror infrastructure directly rather than relying solely on diplomatic pressure, was tested again in 2019, when the Indian Air Force struck a Jaish-e-Mohammed camp in Balakot following the Pulwama attack, marking the first use of air power across the border since 1971.That same resolve was demonstrated at a far larger scale in 2025 during Operation Sindoor, when the armed forces struck targets deep inside Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir over 88 hours, backed by extensive use of modern surveillance and precision-strike capability.

articles.title: Between 1907 and 1928, a Kansas retiree built a home and garden from concrete, leaving more than 150 sculptures now preserved as the Garden of Eden
articles.summary: Explore the Garden of Eden in Lucas, Kansas, a unique retirement project by Samuel Perry Dinsmoor featuring over 200 concrete sculptures that reflect his populist and religious beliefs. This historic site attracts thousands of visitors annually and showcases grassroots art at its finest.
articles.body: Samuel Perry Dinsmoor was a former teacher and Union Army veteran who, after moving from his farm into the little town of Lucas in central Kansas, chose to spend his retirement building a cabin, a garden and a statement about the world. According to the Kansas Historical Society, Dinsmoor created more than 150 concrete sculptures there, many of which reflect his religious views and Populist politics. The site is listed on the National Register of Historic Places, and he worked on it from 1907 to 1928. It is now called the Garden of Eden and is considered one of the best examples of grassroots art in the United States.A stone log cabinDinsmoor was born in Ohio in 1843, according to the Kansas Historical Society. He enlisted in the Union Army in 1862, served three years and saw 18 major battles, including Gettysburg. He then taught school in Illinois for five terms before turning to farming. In 1888 he moved to Russell County, Kansas, spent a spell in Nebraska and was back in Russell County by 1891. He retired from farming in 1905, moved into Lucas and bought a quarter of a block, and that is where the Garden of Eden began.The showpiece was a stone log cabin that was not made of logs at all. Dinsmoor used local post rock limestone, a stone that got its name because farmers carved it into fence posts on a prairie that lacked timber. The Kohler Foundation describes an eleven-room cabin built from that limestone. Dinsmoor's own description mentions a private light plant under the back porch, and local tradition holds that it was the first cabin in Lucas to have electricity.Concrete with a missionAccording to the Kansas Historical Society, Dinsmoor used 113 tons of cement on the garden, and this is where the story moves from architecture to argument. The Kohler Foundation says his sculptures reflect both his Populist ideas and his religious convictions, and both organisations count roughly 150 pieces.According to the National Register nomination, many of the statues sit on concrete trees, some as high as forty feet. A tableau depicts a doctor, a lawyer, a priest, and a banker crucifying labour. Another has a Goddess of Liberty. Life-size representations of Adam and Eve welcomed tourists, though local politicians soon demanded they wear concrete loincloths. Dinsmoor even rigged a speaking tube so he could address curious passersby through the mouth of an angel. He also had a mausoleum erected for himself on the grounds, and visitors can still see him in a coffin with a glass top. Building the garden was demanding work, and Dinsmoor built it to last, molding each figure over steel and chicken wire.Reclaimed from neglectDinsmoor died in 1932. His wife sold the property to pay her taxes, and the garden went to seed. It sat neglected until it was bought and reopened as an attraction in the late 1960s, and it joined the National Register of Historic Places on April 28, 1977. In 2012, the Kohler Foundation sponsored a substantial renovation. Crews stripped away vines and trees, wiped away years of moss and mould, and revealed the original stained concrete. Some figures were also freed of the concrete loincloths the community had once demanded. The Kohler Foundation says the garden now draws more than 10,000 visitors a year to a community of fewer than 500 people.Its meaning has also broadened. The National Trust for Historic Preservation describes a stone log cabin surrounded by tall concrete sculptures that protest against bank trusts and monopolies. The trust adds that Dinsmoor's populist vision has been at the heart of Lucas since 1909, just two years after he began building.The Garden of Eden is near the corner of Kansas and Second Streets in Lucas, along the Post Rock Scenic Byway. There are guided tours that discuss the tales behind the sculptures, and opening hours vary by season, so it's worth checking the official Garden of Eden website before heading out.
